content.text:
## The gradient outline

Velo draws one thin rounded border around the whole screen. Its colour fades diagonally from cyan at the top left to magenta at the bottom right. The panels inside use plain dim borders, so the outer frame is the only bright line on screen.

For Maester:
- **How to draw it:** colour each border cell by its position, using `t = (x/width + y/height) / 2` and blending between two brand colours. The renderer already builds truecolor codes (`38;2;r;g;b`). On 256-colour consoles we round to the nearest palette entry, and with 16 colours or no ANSI we fall back to a plain border.
- **Colours:** use Maester's wordmark colours, red to amber (the game HUD already uses them), so it looks like Maester rather than a copy of Velo's neon. A teal-to-red option could show the run's state.
- **Optional motion:** shift the gradient slowly while tests run, then hold it still when the run finishes. It's cheap because only border cells change.
- **What it costs:** two columns and two rows, so it should only appear when the full-screen dashboard has room for it.

## Ideas worth taking

**Strongest fits**
1. **Status pill and clock in the header.** For example `● RUNNING · contoso.onmicrosoft.com · 18:31:41`, then `✓ COMPLETE`. The dot pulses while work is in progress.
2. **Keycap footer.** Keys like `?` help and `q` quit shown as filled chips along the bottom, with the theme and mode on the right. Today our keys are hidden.
3. **Events panel (`tail -f`).** A timestamped log with a coloured tag per line: `auth` Graph connected · `exo` connected · `skip` 12 tests need E5 · `warn` 429 throttled, retrying · `fail` MT.1005 high. Today the dashboard shows tests but not the run's own events, and this would fill that gap.
4. **Big readout with ghost digits.** A centre number (pass % or tests done) in large block digits, with the unused leading digits drawn dim (`003.8`). The game HUD already has large block digits we can reuse.
5. **Placeholders that hold the layout.** Values show a dim `—` until data arrives, so nothing jumps around when numbers fill in.

**Good fits**
6. **One accent colour per phase.** Velo switches the whole screen's accent (gauge, numbers, bars, chart) as it moves from latency to download to upload. We could give connect, discover, test and report a colour each, or tint by the product being tested.
7. **History panel.** Earlier runs, one per row: date, tenant, pass %, failures, a small bar and a letter grade, with the current run highlighted. It builds on the Drift data we already keep.
8. **Grade badge when the run finishes.** A coloured A–F chip plus a one-line final summary (`✓ FINAL · 412 passed · 23 failed · 3 high`).
9. **Masking for screen sharing.** Velo shows the client IP as `•••.•••`. A redact option (switch or key) could hide the tenant ID, domain and UPNs for demos and recordings.
10. **Timeline chart.** A dotted area chart of tests per second (or pass and fail over time) whose y-axis rescales as the run goes. It would sit next to or replace the Pace chart.

**Polish**
11. A `◆` accent glyph before each panel title.
12. Border badges that double as hints, like Velo's "s to change". We already have `Badge`, so this is mostly a change of wording.
13. A small reverse-video logo chip at the top left.
14. A `t` theme key: Maester default, high contrast and mono, which also helps accessibility.

**I'd leave out** the arc gauge made of braille dots. It looks great for a single speed number, but Maester's progress is better shown by the track and product lanes we already have.

I built the status pill (1), the ◆ glyph before panel titles (11), and single-click links on macOS. The work is on a new branch, `feat/console-status-pill`, cut from `main`. Nothing is committed yet, and I haven't tried a click in your own terminal.

**Status pill (1).** The top row of the right column now shows the current phase, the tenant domain and the time, for example `● RUN TESTS · contoso.com · 17:47:26`. The dot blinks every half second. When the column is narrow, the domain is dropped first, then the time. On narrow consoles with no right column there's no pill, because the header already shows the phases there.

**◆ before panel titles (11).** The diamond takes the panel's own colour (green for Products, red for Failed so far, teal for Running), or Maester orange on neutral panels. It costs two columns. At 165 columns the insight panels don't have room for both the diamond and their badge ("73%", "pass · fail"), so they keep the badge and skip the diamond.

**Single-click links.** No terminal can make a hyperlink open on a plain click by itself; Cmd-click is how they work. So while the tests run, the dashboard asks the terminal to report mouse clicks and opens the clicked link itself:
- A left click with no modifier, pressed and released on the same cell, opens the link with `open` (or `xdg-open` on Linux).
- The status bar hint changes from "⌘-click to open" to "click to open" while this is on.
- Mouse reporting switches off when the tests finish and when the dashboard closes or the process exits. Any clicks still waiting are thrown away so they don't show up at your prompt as junk text.
- It's off on Windows, whose console reports the mouse differently.
- **Trade-off:** while the tests run, selecting text needs Option held. After the run, selection and Cmd-click work as before.

**How I checked it:**
- The console tests pass, plus two new ones: one for the pill, and one for clicks (drags, other buttons and modifier keys open nothing).
- The full `./powershell/tests/pester.ps1` run passes: 136 files.
- I ran a live dashboard in a pseudo-terminal and sent it real mouse reports. The click on `maester.dev` opened that link, a click on a cell with no link did nothing, and no input was left over after the run.
- The image above is rendered from a real dashboard frame.

Most of the code is in [MtConsoleRenderer.Input.cs](src/Maester.Engine/MtConsoleRenderer.Input.cs). The pill is in [MtConsoleRenderer.cs](src/Maester.Engine/MtConsoleRenderer.cs), the glyph in `Box` in [MtConsoleRenderer.Panels.cs](src/Maester.Engine/MtConsoleRenderer.Panels.cs), and the switch that turns clicks on is in [Write-MtConsoleLine.ps1](powershell/internal/session/Write-MtConsoleLine.ps1). Run it from the repo in a real terminal (iTerm2, Terminal.app or Ghostty) rather than the app's terminal panel, so the mouse behaves like it will for users.

1. Build and import your local copy. This loads the new engine DLL from `powershell/lib`:

```bash
cd ~/github/maester && pwsh -NoExit -Command "./build/Build-LocalMaester.ps1"
```

2. In that same pwsh session, connect and run. The full-screen dashboard is the default (`-Verbosity None`) and needs a window at least 80×16. Make it wide, around 160 columns or more, so the right column appears and the pill shows above it:

```powershell
Connect-Maester
Invoke-Maester -Path ./tests/maester -OutputFolder ./TestResults
```

If you'd rather not touch a tenant, keep `Connect-Maester` out. Most tests then skip, but the dashboard still runs and you can still check the pill, the diamonds and the clicks.

**What to try while the tests run:**
- **Pill:** the top right should show `● RUN TESTS · yourdomain.com · hh:mm:ss`, with the dot blinking.
- **Diamonds:** each panel title has a `◆` in the panel's colour.
- **Clicks:** the bottom bar should say "click to open". A plain click on `maester.dev`, `Docs` or `Star on GitHub` should open your browser. A link in the right column (the blog post or the featured contributor) should open the same way.
- **Selection:** dragging to select text needs Option held while the tests run.
- **After the run:** once the tests finish, mouse reporting is off again. Cmd-click and normal selection should work, and no stray `[<0;…M` text should appear at your prompt.

If the clicks do nothing in your terminal, check that mouse reporting is allowed. In Terminal.app it's under View → Allow Mouse Reporting; iTerm2 has a matching setting in the profile's Terminal tab.

Ideas borrowed from a speed-test TUI for the full-screen dashboard.

## What changes

- **Status pill.** The right column starts with the status of the run, at its right edge: the current phase with a dot that pulses, the tenant domain and the time (`● RUN TESTS · contoso.com · 18:31:41`). The domain goes first when the column is short of room, then the time. No pill without a right column.
- **◆ before panel titles,** in the panel's colour (green Products, red Failed, teal Running) or the wordmark orange on neutral panels. It costs two columns, so a box that has no room for it next to its badge keeps the badge and leaves the diamond out (the insight panels at 165 columns).
- **Underlined links.** `Hyperlink` underlines the text, so every link on the dashboard reads as one (blog post, contributor, update notice, drift date). In the status bar the words of a linked label are underlined, not the padding.
- **One-click links (macOS and Linux).** While the tests run, the dashboard asks the terminal for mouse reports (SGR, modes 1000/1006) and opens the link under a plain left click itself (`open` / `xdg-open`). The status bar drops its "⌘-click to open" hint while that works.

  - Trade-off: while the tests run, selecting text needs Option (macOS) or Shift held. After the run, selection and Cmd/Ctrl-click work as before.
  - Off on Windows, whose console reports the mouse another way. `ClickLinks` is set by `Write-MtConsoleLine.ps1` when the dashboard reads keys.
